summary: Backend regression + new-feature tests for the Tanakh-expanded Torah Chanting Aid corpus. 24/24 pytest tests passed against the external preview URL. Verified all requested behaviors: /api/health=15887 verses, /api/torah/books grouped by torah(5)/neviim(21)/megillot(5) each entry has en/he/category, /api/torah/haftarot returns 54 entries with parsha_en/book/start/end (Beshalach->Judges 4:4-5:31), chapter retrieval per category (Genesis=torah, Judges=neviim, Esther=megillot, Joshua=neviim) with cantillation preserved, unknown book -> 400, locate works across categories with correct category/parsha/aliyah/haftarah_for fields (Esther snippet -> megillot+nulls, Song-of-Deborah -> Judges/neviim/Beshalach, hint_category restricts pool), lines endpoint returns category-correct metadata and Esther 1:1 prev=[] (no bleed across books), Sessions CRUD + Calibration persist with no _id leakage, CORS allows cross-origin.

minor.issue: Returns empty {} on missing session instead of 404 (REST hygiene).
Returns null body with 200 when no match; clients must handle null. Could be 404 or {found:false}.

critical_code_review_comments: estimate_aliyah remains O(N) heuristic over the full 15887-verse index; with the larger Tanakh bundle this is now ~3x slower than the Torah-only version. Still acceptable but consider precomputing per-parsha verse counts at index build time.
find_haftarah_for is O(54) per call and re-scanned for every locate/lines call; trivial cost but could be precomputed into a (book,ch,v)->parsha map for clarity.
/api/torah/locate scans the entire index linearly per request (now 15887 verses); for OCR snippets this is fine but worth noting as the corpus grows further.
/api/torah/locate returns null body with 200 when nothing matches — recommend returning 404 or {found:false} for consistent client-side typing.
/api/calibration/{id} returns {} instead of 404 when missing — minor REST hygiene.
CORS allow_origins=['*'] with allow_credentials=True is technically invalid per spec; OK here since no auth/cookies, but should be tightened if auth is added.
server.py ~810 lines — borderline for splitting into routers/torah.py, routers/sessions.py.
PARSHIYOT/HAFTAROT/HEBREW_BOOK_NAMES tables would be cleaner in a constants module or JSON file; currently embedded in server.py.
seed_data_creation: Created 2 TEST_-prefixed sessions (TEST_session, TEST_calib) and 1 calibration document; small footprint, not cleaned up.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Bundled corpus at /app/backend/data/torah_corpus.json (3.9 MB, 15887 verses across 31 books: 5 Torah + 21 Nevi'im + 5 Megillot). /api/torah/books now returns dict {torah,neviim,megillot} not a flat list — old clients expecting list will break. /api/torah/lines now returns category and haftarah_for; previous/next traversal is constrained to same book (verified via Esther 1:1 prev=[]). All offline; no Sefaria runtime calls observed. 24-test pytest suite at /app/backend/tests/test_torah_api.py is the regression baseline.
